newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - July 28.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Workplace Relations Minister Peter Reith yesterday said the recent leaking of government documents on the South Pacific had been blown out of proportion and should be treated with more levity. Reith commended New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peter for dismissing the documents as irrelevant. Page 3.

A government spokesman said yesterday the cabinet meeting on unemployment, scheduled for August 5, would only be held if Prime Minister John Howard had recovered from pneumonia. Howard is expected to remain in hospital for most of this week. Treasurer Peter Costello and Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith have both blamed Howard's condition on his schedule. Page 3.

A Council of Small Business Organisations of Australia report, commissioned by the Department of Transport and Regional Development, says state and federal governments should look beyond savings to a department when regional offices are closed and consider the total economic impact of such decisions. Page 3.

Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions Brian Martin told the Perth Court of Criminal Appeal on Friday that Alan Bond's four-year sentence for corporate fraud was so disproportionate to his conduct that the trial judge must have erred. Martin argued that Bond's crime represented the most serious category of fraud, and the sentence should therefore be increased. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A record 90,119 people filled the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Saturday night for the second Bledisloe Cup match and watched the Australian Wallabies lose 33-18 in a game dominated by the New Zealand All Blacks. Kiwi captain Sean Fitzpatrick and Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett support the idea of having the game in Melbourne again despite the Wallabies' disappointing performance and a lack of crowd involvement in the game. Page 1.

The federal cabinet has split, fearing an international backlash over Attorney-General Daryl Williams' plan to abolish the Sex Discrimination Commissioner. Pressure from the ministry has forced Williams to withdraw his submission on a restructuing of the Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission but he will still seek a cabinet decision tomorrow on whether current commission president Sir Ronald Wilson should have his term extended. Page 1.

A confidante of Prime Minister John Howard says he is likely to chair the cabinet meeting on unemployment next Tuesday despite a bout of pneumonia that has put him in hospital. Medical experts say it will take Howard two weeks to recover and he is curretly seeing only immediate family and most senior advisers. Page 1.

Australian Maccabiah games officials have instigated tests on the Yarkon River in Tel Aviv - the scene of the Israeli bridge collapse two weeks ago - following the death of a third Australian on Saturday. Melbourne bridge player Elizabeth Sawicki died of multiple organ failure, believed to be the result of complications arising from pollution poisoning. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Two police investigations, arising from the deaths of two men who were bludgeoned outside a Kings Cross restaurant early this year have found that Korean gangs involved in extortion, loan-sharking and threats of violence are operating virtually unchecked at the Sydney Harbour Casino and in the suburbs of Sydney. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has refused to embark on a project to revamp the structure of the Reserve Bank of Australia, saying conflicts of interest by board members are unavoidable. His comments indicate that he is not worried by two potential parliamentary inquiries into inherent conflicts of interest within the Reserve Bank board. Page 1.

Acting Prime Minister Peter Costello says Prime Minister John Howard's stay in hospital because of a bout of pneumonia will not affect Howard's long-term leadership. Howard's illness has brought attention to the Liberal leadership but all contenders are affirming the security of Howard's position. Page 2.

The Dean of Architecture at the University of Sydney, Neville Quarry, says the New South Wales Government is timid in its approach to architecture in comparison to the Victorian government. Quarry commented on the state government's attitude when judging the interntional design competition for Melbourne's Federation Square. Page 1.
THE AGE

A A$328 million transformation of Melbourne will be designed by the London-based Lab Architectural Studio following its win in the Federation Square design competition with a plan that features a 3.2 hectare square spanning the Jolimont rail yards with clsters of buildings. Page 1.

The National Gallery of Victoria's entire collection of Australian art will be housed in the new Museum of Modern Art to be built as part of the Federation Square redevelopment. National Gallery of Victoria director Timothy Potts said the new museum was the most significant development in Australian art since the establishment of the National Gallery in Canberra. Page 1.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett has criticised the Melbourne Cricket Club for saving seats for members who did not turn up to Saturday night's Bledisloe Cup match at the MCG, while thousands of fans were told the ground was sold out. Kennett believes a deadline should be imposed on members who wish to attend events so their seats can be sold if they don't turn up. Page A1.

The two Liberal ministers who are potential candidates for the prime ministership should John Howard prove too unhealthy -- Workplace Relations Minister Peter Reith and Treasurer Peter Costello -- have asserted Howard has their loyalty and believe he will quickly recover from his illness. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
